Varasiddhi Vinayaka, Chokkanathar (Shiva), Meenakshi Amman, Kali, Bhairava, Shanmuga (subsidiary sannidhis)

history.period: c. 1890s (thatched shed); expanded and renovated through the 20th century (Wikipedia's 'completed 1865' date conflicts with the 1890s origin story - verify)
history.summary: One of Chennai's most visited Murugan temples, considered a northern replica of the Palani Murugan temple ('Vada' = north + 'Palani'). Per the sthalapurana, Murugan devotee Annasamy Nayagar built a simple thatched shed around 1890 and kept a Murugan painting there for personal worship; his utterances in divine possession ('arul vakku') reportedly cured diseases and arranged marriages, drawing devotees, and donations turned the shed into a grand temple. It was renovated in the 1920s when the rajagopuram was built. Around 7,000 couples are married here each year, and its popularity is partly credited to the patronage of cinema stars. The temple tank lies in front; the eastern tower rises 40.8 m and carries stucco figures from the Skanda Purana along with the 108 Bharatanatyam dance gestures. A golden chariot is used in festivals. Maintained by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.

name: Vadapalani Murugan Temple
town_description: Vadapalani is a busy commercial and residential neighbourhood in west Chennai on Arcot Road, anchored by the Vadapalani Metro station (Blue Line) at the junction. It grew from a suburban settlement around the temple into one of the city's main shopping and entertainment hubs.

travel.railway: Chennai Central - about 8 km; Vadapalani Metro station (Blue Line) is adjacent to the temple (verify).
travel.road: Palani Andavar Koil Street, Vadapalani, Chennai 600026; on Arcot Road, served by city buses and metro.

visitor_information.best_time: January-February (Thaipusam) and October-November (Skanda Shashti); Fridays and Tuesdays draw larger crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00 PM-9:30 PM (some sources report evening close at 9:00 PM - verify). Entry free; e-hundi facility available.
